blocks.heading: Hair in the brush, fine roots, a parting that shows more scalp
quotes: “Every wash I end up with a handful of hair.”
“I bought a hair oil, it ran down my forehead and onto my hands, and I gave up after a few days.”

explainer.heading: Most of the hair that falls out in the shower was ready to fall
body: Losing a few dozen hairs a day is normal. Skip washing for a few days and those hairs come out together, so it looks like more than it is.
What you can do at home is keep the scalp clean and moisturised, and pull less on the hair when brushing and washing. Peel Ion is the last care step, rolled straight onto the scalp after washing.
Hair falling out in patches, sudden heavy shedding, or an itchy red scalp: see a doctor before buying any product.

blocks.heading: Who it suits, who should wait

items.heading: Fine hair that breaks when brushed
items.body: Use after washing to care for the scalp and roots. With regular use, hair looks thicker and stronger.

items.heading: A scalp that feels dry or slightly itchy after washing
items.body: Glycerin, panthenol and Pentavitin are humectants. Roll on a thin layer and massage gently.

items.heading: Hair falling out in patches or suddenly
items.body: A dermatologist needs to find the cause first. A care product does not replace an examination.

items.heading: A scraped, inflamed or wounded scalp
items.body: Wait until the scalp has fully healed. The roller balls would rub over the damaged skin.

rows.name: Redensyl™
rows.role: A branded active commonly used in scalp and hair-root care products.

rows.name: Glycerin
rows.role: Humectant; keeps the scalp from feeling tight and dry.

rows.name: Panthenol
rows.role: Provitamin B5; moisturises the scalp and hair.

rows.name: Pentavitin™
rows.role: A sugar-based moisturising complex that binds to the skin surface.

rows.name: Pomelo peel oil
rows.role: Fragrance; a familiar hair care ingredient in Vietnam.
rows.suitedFor: People who like the scent; patch-test if sensitive to essential oils

blocks.heading: How to use it

items.heading: Wash, then towel off
items.body: Use after washing. Towel the hair until it is just damp, or let it dry.

items.heading: Unlock so the essence reaches the roller
items.body: Open the cap so the essence flows down to the three balls, then lock it again. This keeps the amount under control.

items.heading: Part the hair and roll along the scalp
items.body: Work section by section, rolling along the scalp and roots. Massage gently for 3–5 minutes.

items.heading: Leave it in
items.body: No need to wash it out. If you blow-dry, use the cool setting.

blocks.footnote: Frequency per the brand's instruction graphic: daily if hair is weak and noticeably thin; every other day if it is only slightly weak.

items.q: What does “ion” in the name mean?
items.a: The brand calls the three metal roller balls an ion roller. We have no separate data on what the “ion” part does, so we only describe what you can see: the balls put the essence on the scalp and give a light massage as you roll.

items.q: Can I use it if I am shedding a lot of hair?
items.a: Peel Ion is a cosmetic scalp care product, not a medicine. If hair is falling out in patches, suddenly, or the scalp is red and itchy, see a dermatologist first.
Yes. The brand states it is for both men and women.
The brand places Peel Ion after Hair Boost shampoo: wash, rinse well, towel off, then roll on. Another shampoo works too, as long as the scalp is clean.
Lock the roller and close the cap after use. Keep in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight and out of reach of children.

blocks.heading: The steps before the roller
blocks.intro: Peel Ion comes last. Before it: washing, a hair mask, and now and then a deeper scalp cleanse.
